item.title: Tenerife return to action after death of De Miguel
item.description: Tenefire fans display a banner paying tribute to Jesus de Miguel [Getty Images] Tenerife played their first game since the death of striker Jesus de Miguel on an emotional day at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium. De Miguel died at the age of 30 on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a home match in Spain's Segunda Division. Tenerife beat bottom side Ceuta 2-0 on Sunday, with tributes to De Miguel paid both before and during the game. Lengthy standing ovations preceded and followed a minute of silence before the match. In the ninth minute play was stopped and a round of applause took place, while a video of De Miguel was shown in the stadium, as happened at all first- and second-tier games in Spain last weekend. Tenerife fans displayed a banner that read: "Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally blue and white." Forward Nacho Gil opened the scoring for the home side in the 40th minute and celebrated by holding up De Miguel's shirt. Gil revealed a message written under his shirt that read: "Demi, always in our hearts." Neal Viereck scored four minutes from time as Tenerife ended a run of six games without a win. They are 14th in the table. Tenerife's game with Granada on 7 November was postponed and the club invited fans to the stadium to pay their respects to De Miguel. Owono was given a 12-match suspension by the Spanish football federation for the challenge which resulted in De Miguel's death. The federation has ruled that the game between Tenerife and Andorra, which was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after the incident occurred, will not be replayed and the 2-2 score will stand. Tenerife's Enric Gallego carried a wreath of flowers on to the pitch [Getty Images] Tenerife boss says Owono's 12-match ban 'feels light' Owono undecided over future following De Miguel death 'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono

item.title: Players of the game from FSU's scrappy win over Pittsburgh
item.description: The Florida State Seminoles played the Pittsburgh Panthers a scrappy defensive performance, winning 16-10 against one of the ACC's better teams They are now 5-5 on the season, including 3-4 in ACC play, one game away from bowl eligibility. It's strange to say, but this team can finish out an up-and-down 2026 season at 8-5 if everything goes right for them. It was another awe-inspiring defensive performance by FSU, which has put Ernie Sims and his company squarely on fans' radar, in a good way. On X, "I don’t care who FSU brings in at head coach. Ernie Sims MUST be on staff," one user said . "He’s completely transformed a defense that was depleted and defeated in under two weeks. His energy is undeniable," another tweeted . Florida State has won two in a row after posting three-straight losses. Now, their schedule has them returning to Doak Campbell to take on the NC State Wolfpack , and in the regular season finale, the Florida Gators . Anything is, in fact, possible with this new staff and new energy in the building. Yes, this is what hope feels like, Seminoles fans. With all of this in mind, here are our players of the game. WR Jasen Lopez The two-sport phenom was responsible for having the most receiving yards on the Seminoles with 72 on five receptions. His longest was a 46-yard reception that put FSU at Pitt's 10-yard-line, which ultimately set up a Gabe Panikowski field goal. And speaking of... K Gabe Panikowski The talk about Panikowski has been rather quiet, but he has quietly built one of the best seasons a FSU kicker has had in recent memory, perhaps even better than the great Ryan Fitzgerald in terms of efficiency. Simply because he has not missed a kick all year. He is just one of two players in the nation with a perfect percentage on field goals. He is also perfect on extra point attempts. If he keeps this up, he could find himself in consideration for the Lou Groza award. RB Amari Thomas Thomas was responsible for FSU's lone touchdown of the day, a one-yard run that put them up 13-7; without it, Florida State may lose this game. But they did not, and for that reason, I have to give Thomas his flowers, who, also has stepped up admirably in the wake of several injuries to the starters. item.title: France manager Zinedine Zidane ‘irritated’ by rumours of a rift with Kylian Mbappé
item.description: France manager Zinedine Zidane ‘irritated’ by rumours of a rift with Kylian Mbappé Whilst he has mostly been seen with a grin from ear to ear and a twinkle in his eye since his appointment as manager of France, it was with a stern expression that Zinedine Zidane, speaking to the press ahead of the match against Turkey, broke his silence to address certain gossip. When asked about rumours suggesting he has a strained relationship with his captain, Kylian Mbappé (27), the French legend was keen to set the record straight. “I don’t really understand (these rumours). I’m not going to get into the debate; our relationship is going perfectly,” assured the former number 10. “For the player (he didn’t mention his name) as well as for me. I can’t stop people from saying what they say.” When asked again whether the reports in the press had annoyed him, Zidane did not beat about the bush in giving his view of the matter. “Yes, the things I hear, inevitably, are rather irritating,” he said, with a touch of bitterness. In recent weeks, there have been several reports of misunderstandings between the two men. Mbappé, who started on the left wing against Turkey in September, is said to have been frustrated by this tactical choice, as he prefers to play centrally. item.title: How England can top their Nations League group against Spain - and why it matters
item.description: How England can top their Nations League group against Spain - and why it matters England will finish top of their Nations League group if they beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday, and the scoreline does not matter. The Three Lions trail the world champions by three points in the group, with Spain boasting a perfect record of five wins from five games. La Roja's win against Czechia last week extended their record-breaking unbeaten run to 43 games. Spain have not lost in any competition since a friendly defeat to Colombia in March 2024. England are already through to the quarter-finals. A 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley, settled by a Harry Kane penalty on his record-breaking 126th appearance, guaranteed a top-two finish in League A Group 3. Why any win is enough Thomas Tuchel's were beaten 3-2 by Spain at Wembley in September. Even so, their overall goal difference is better than Spain's, so a victory of any margin would lift them above Luis de la Fuente's side. A draw or a defeat would leave England in second place. The quarter-finals are two-legged ties. The four League A group winners are seeded for the draw and will meet a runner-up from a different group. That should mean a kinder draw on paper, although the current runners-up show the limits of that idea: Greece in Group A2, Denmark in Group A4 and France in Group A1. The bigger advantage is the second leg. Group winners host it, which would give England the chance to settle the tie at Wembley. Finish second, and they would be unseeded, drawn against a group winner and forced to play the decisive leg away from home. Who England could face in the Nations League quarter-finals? Teams from the same group cannot be paired in the quarter-finals, so England will not meet Spain again at that stage. With one round of games left in every group, these sides remain in the running elsewhere in League A: Portugal have already booked their place in the last eight. The other groups will be settled in the final round of fixtures.

item.title: Yankees bring back Tim Hill on a one-year contract
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 06: Tim Hill #54 of the New York Yankees pitches against the Boston Red Sox during the fifth inning at Yankee Stadium on July 06, 2024 in in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you said the Yankees’ first transaction of the offseason would be to re-sign one of their relievers, that’d be pretty believable, but you’d probably assume it’d be David Bednar off his qualifying offer. Instead, it’s a bit of a surprise, as the Yankees have re-signed lefty Tim Hill to a cheap, one-year deal with a club option in 2028. Hill has had a classic reliever career. A 32nd-round pick in 2014, he debuted with the Royals in 2018, was traded to the Padres for one-time Yankee Franchy Cordero in 2020, and spent the next few seasons carving out a niche as a funky lefty for San Diego until he appeared to hit a wall in 2023. Over the next year and a half, he pitched to a 5.60 ERA over 67 innings for two teams and was released in June 2024 by the dreadful White Sox. Left-handed reliever Tim Hill and the New York Yankees are in agreement on a one-year, $2.25 million contract that includes a $2.5 million club option for 2028, sources tell ESPN. Hill returns for his fourth season with the Yankees, whose bullpen is a top priority this offseason. — Jeff Passan (@JeffPassan) November 15, 2026 Being 34 at the time, in a position with such volatile turnover, that could’ve well been it for Hill, but the Yankees gave him a shot on a flier two days later and found something in him, tweaking his arsenal and turning him into one of the most effective lefty specialists in the sport, spinning a 2.05 ERA in 44 innings down the stretch. He had gained so much trust in such little time that he owns a place in Yankees lore for being unjustly left in the bullpen in Game 1 of the World Series in favor of a rusty, injured Nestor Cortes. Hill was worse, but still effective in 2025, though the warning signs started to flash. As a high-80s sinker-throwing lefty who relies on location with his extremely low arm angle, he’s susceptible to giving up hard contact if his command is off. In 2024, he had some of the best damage prevention stats in the sport, but it has slowly eroded since. 2026 was a disaster for Hill, pitching to a 4.60 ERA and 5.93 FIP in 58.2 innings as his chase rate plummeted and he became completely unplayable against righties, allowing a .293/.365/.543 slashline in 104 plate appearances. That, coupled with the presence of Brent Headrick, Ryan Weathers, and Ryan Yarbrough, left him off the playoff roster for both rounds. Yet, despite the 36-year-old’s worst season peripherally, he had a strong market, drawing interest from teams like the Dodgers, Mets, and Guardians. Ultimately, he decided to stay with the team that revitalized his career on a low-risk contract. item.title: Patriots QB Drake Maye knocked out of game vs. Lions
item.description: MUNICH, Germany — The New England Patriots weren't the only team to lose one of its most important players in a game with the Detroit Lions at Allianz Stadium in Munich, Germany, on Sunday, Nov. 15. On the sack by Aidan Hutchinson that preceded his celebration-induced knee injury, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury that knocked him out of the game. Hutchinson appeared to use a hip-drop tackle to bring down the 2025 MVP runner-up and landed on Maye's ankle while finishing the tackle. Maye was immediately removed from the game as the Patriots took a 3-0 lead via field goal at 9:15 in the opening quarter. The Patriots drove 70 yards on the opening drive but got stuck in the mud after backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was inserted. On its next six drives to close the first half, the Patriots netted negative 1 yard on offense. DeVito was four-for-nine passing for 16 yards, plus an interception with 51 seconds to go in the second quarter. After Lions quarterback Jared Goff threw his second interception of the half on the ensuing Lions drive, Detroit carried a 21-3 lead into halftime. nbianchi@detroitnews.com @nolanbianchi This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Patriots QB Drake Maye knocked out of game vs. Lions

item.title: U.S. women's hockey team makes World Championship final for 25th consecutive time
item.description: The U.S. women's hockey team is now 25 for 25 in making World Championship finals. The reigning Olympic and world champion beat Finland 5-0 in the semifinals on Sunday in Denmark, setting up another possible showdown with rival Canada in Monday's final. Canada plays Sweden in the second semifinal later Sunday. The Americans are 6-0 at these worlds, winning every game by at least five goals. Since the start of the 2025 Worlds, the U.S. has won 20 consecutive games between World Championship and Olympic play, a program record. On Sunday, captain Hilary Knight led the way with one goal and one assist, while Aerin Frankel stopped all 13 Finland shots. Earlier in the tournament, the U.S. broke the record for most shots in a single women's worlds game, registering 85 in a 14-0 quarterfinal win over Denmark on Friday. The U.S. had the previous record of 82 from 1997. The 14 goals marked the most for the U.S. in a worlds game since 2000. Frankel broke the American goalie record for most career game wins in worlds history. Frankel is now up to 20 victories, bettering Jessie Vetter's old record of 16. item.description: MIAMI, FLORIDA - MARCH 14: Teruaki Sato #7 of Team Japan hits a double during the third inning against Team Venezuela at the 2026 World Baseball Classic at loanDepot park on March 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have been doing this for a few years now: looking at the top free agents, using the contract Ben Clemens suggests he’ll get, and asking whether you would like the Jays to give him that contract. This year, the lockout makes it a little more complicated. Keith Law’s list is here . Ben Clemens’ is here. Number 5 on Ben Clemens list and number 2 on Keith Law’s is Teruaki Sato. The Jays are said to be talking to him, thinking that he could play outfield. He is a 27-year-old (28 in early March), left-handed hitter. Last year, for the Hanshin Tigers, he hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs, 68 walks, and 164 strikeouts. He’s had six seasons in the NPB, playing 803 games, with a .273/.338/.516, with 167 home runs. Law said: Sato is the best player coming over from NPB this winter and might be the best position-player free agent on the market, period. Playing in a pitcher-friendly stadium in Koshien, Sato hit 79 homers the past two seasons and heads to the posting system off a .306/.383/.609 season, where he also hit 40 doubles and walked more than 10 percent of the time, finishing third in the Central League with 68 walks. It’s easily plus power, earning comparisons to that of Munetaka Murakami, who offered a little more power but less of a hit tool than Sato has. Sato does strike out quite a bit, with a 26.7 percent rate last year, and he had the highest swinging-strike rate of any qualifying NPB hitter. Scouts I’ve asked say his approach is better than the raw data would indicate, that he’s swinging harder and more often to try to do damage, since that’s the expectation given where he’s hit in the lineup and since his home park is unfriendly to power. Between that and the contact question, I wouldn’t be comfortable relying on Sato as a difference-maker for a likely playoff team; there are just too many fail cases. Yousuf urged the youngsters to remain respectful and composed in both victory and defeat, saying that true sportsmanship is reflected in how players conduct themselves on the field, irrespective of the result. item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers scrambles against Grady Jarrett #50 of the Chicago Bears during the second quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield when they return from their bye week to face the Detroit Lions. According to a report from ESPN , citing multiple sources who spoke with NFL Network, Mayfield is dealing with a foot and ankle injury suffered during Tampa Bay’s 27-24 loss to the Chicago Bears last Sunday. The veteran quarterback has reportedly been in and out of a walking boot in recent days to rest and rehabilitate the injury. Fortunately for Tampa Bay, its bye week provided Mayfield with additional recovery time before the team’s upcoming trip to Detroit. The injury occurred during a difficult fourth quarter for Mayfield, who took several hits and was slow to get up on multiple occasions. On one play, Bears defensive lineman Austin Booker briefly grabbed Mayfield’s helmet before a sack, resulting in a face mask penalty. Two plays later, defensive linemen Grady Jarrett and Jeffery Simmons combined to bring Mayfield down awkwardly, leaving the quarterback on the ground for several moments. Despite the apparent discomfort, Mayfield remained in the game and even converted a two-point attempt with his legs to tie the score at 24 with 2:51 remaining. Chicago ultimately kicked the game-winning field goal on its ensuing possession, preventing Tampa Bay’s offense from getting another opportunity. The latest injury adds to an already challenging season for Mayfield, who missed three games earlier this year after dislocating his right thumb during a Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels started in Mayfield’s absence and would be the likely replacement should the veteran be unable to play against Detroit. There is some encouraging news for the Buccaneers, however. According to the report, Mayfield’s foot and ankle injury is not believed to be a long-term concern, and any potential absence is expected to be brief. A stint on injured reserve is not being considered. Mayfield has also not been ruled out against the Lions. Sources familiar with the situation pointed to his history of playing through injuries, suggesting that if his availability comes down to managing pain rather than limited functionality, the quarterback will make every effort to suit up. For a Buccaneers team sitting at 3-6 and just half a game out of first place in the NFC South, having Mayfield available could be crucial as Tampa Bay looks to turn its season around. The team will monitor his recovery when practices resume this week, with his participation potentially offering a clearer indication of whether he’ll be ready for Detroit. The Buccaneers and Lions are scheduled to kick off Sunday, November 22, at 1 p.m. ET.

item.title: Triumph or flop? The Rugby League World Cup that split opinion
item.description: The winning captains: Australia's Isabelle Kelly, her men's counterpart Isaah Yeo and England wheelchair skipper Lewis King [Getty Images] Has the 2026 Rugby League World Cup been a success or not? It depends on who you listen to - and perhaps where in the world you are. The men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments provided plenty of stories - from Kalyn Ponga's return from a broken arm in 23 days, to Jodie Cunningham's mangled ear, to the England wheelchair team's golden ladder, to the men's group format that caused widespread bafflement. But was the World Cup a triumph? The northern and southern hemisphere perspectives provide contrasting answers. For the fourth tournament running, Australia won the men's and women's titles, with New Zealand unable to deliver a twist in either final. Tonga and Samoa brought vibrancy and passion - performing to a level that underlined why they are being elevated to Tier One status. The large Polynesian population in the USA - which will co-host the 2030 men's and women's World Cups - is likely to be key in spreading the rugby league word further around the world. England's Wheelchair World Cup win, in a thunderous final against their old foes France, offset some of the disappointment felt when Brian McDermott's men and Stuart Barrow's women went home early. And unlike when the game was emerging from post-pandemic constraints in 2022, the tournament has also worked financially by posting a profit. "This whole tournament's been incredible," said Australia men's captain Isaah Yeo. "Not just the fans here for New Zealand and Australia, but just everyone. I thought it was all outstanding. "I think it's to date the most competitive and the best World Cup there's been. I think that's only going to continue to grow." That sentiment has been endorsed repeatedly by Australian television broadcaster Channel Seven, which paid a reported A$12m (£6.1m) for exclusive domestic free-to-air coverage of the men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments. Not everyone has been able to feel that positivity, though. The decision to cut the men's tournament from 16 teams to 10 reduced the overall number of matches - and deprived teams such as Jamaica and Greece of a chance to build on the feelgood factor they provided as debutants in 2022. That decision was made after Australia stepped in to stage the tournament, postponed for a year when scheduled hosts France pulled out for financial reasons. item.description: Credit: Is She Game? Podcast The 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup figures to be one of the top sports stories of the year, with a more level playing field among the best teams and the USWNT hungry to avenge their early exit in 2023. The Women’s World Cup will also be an experiment to see whether Netflix can successfully broadcast a big live sports tournament. The streamer has exclusive broadcast rights to the World Cup in the U.S. and Canada . Previously, Fox had the rights to the tournament, making accessibility a pretty easy question to answer — games would be available to watch on Fox and its affiliated channels. Streaming is a bit of a different beast. Looking ahead to the event, breakout women’s sports personality Coach Jackie J is calling on Netflix to expand access to the games. So far, Netflix has not developed a plan to make the World Cup available in bars, restaurants and other commercial establishments — a common problem as streamers air more sports, and one that could hamper the momentum coming off the World Cup we just had in North America last summer. “I have heard from owners of sports bars across the country, multiple different people messaging me, saying they’re worried they won’t be able to host any watch parties for one of the biggest women’s sports events of all time,” Coach Jackie said this week on her podcast, Is She Game? “Why? Because Netflix has the sole rights to the Women’s World Cup in 2027, and they’re a subscription service. And that is technically unavailable to commercial establishments. There’s no commercial licensing situation set up right now.” Technically, it is illegal for bar or restaurant owners to show games through a personal streaming login. Companies like EverPass Media work as intermediaries , striking deals with streamers and then charging restaurant owners to air streaming games legally in their buildings. Some streamers offer standalone subscriptions for businesses. These commercial subscriptions can cost hundreds per month, on top of traditional cable. But businesses can be fined thousands if they show games illegally. The problem has already cropped up as Prime Video and Peacock bought exclusive rights to big sporting events like NFL playoff games in recent years. Netflix’s ownership of the World Cup will be among the most prominent case studies. item.title: The blueprint for how the Cowboys can beat the 49ers
item.description: Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images | Getty Images The 4-5 Dallas Cowboys have a big opportunity to narrow the gap for first place in the NFC East when they take on the 7-1 San Francisco 49ers at AT&T Stadium this week. Here are three keys to a Cowboys victory. Flip the script Dallas ranks near the bottom of the NFL in run defense. The 49ers possess one of the league’s best rushing attacks behind Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, and the mobility of quarterback Brock Purdy. The Cowboys defense has the NFL’s worst third-down defense at nearly a 50% conversion rate allowed. San Francisco has the second highest third-down conversion rate. If Dallas is to stand a chance this week, something has to give. This defense can make an impact on their third-down conversion rate by limiting the run on first and second down. Forcing Brock Purdy to throw the ball on third-and-long throughout the day is one of the reasons Atlanta was able to steal one against this team. The largest reason for the 49ers success on the ground is due to the brilliant scheme put together by Kyle Shanahan. One of the keys in beating this scheme is to watch fullback Kyle Juszczyk. The defensive line and linebackers cannot allow all of the movement before and after the snap confuse them. The 49ers love to run the ball behind their beloved fullback. He’ll line up wide at the X, move into the backfield, and end up at the wing all in the same play before the snap. They’ll also motion him out of the backfield out wide to use him as a blocker on a screen. If Dallas is to stand a chance at flipping the script, they’ll need to pay full attention to Juszczyk. Play the cleanest game of the year This key may be obvious, but it’s perhaps the most important one of the day. When this team finds success on offense, defense and special teams, they simply cannot afford to gift those plays back to the 49ers. Dallas has to deliver consistent jabs throughout the day and connect on the big swings when the opportunities are there. What could already be a long day for the Cowboys will undoubtedly be compounded by self-inflicted mistakes if they can’t get out of their own way. When the all-too-often third-down offsides penalties, holding calls on big run plays, and untimely personal fouls crop up, the 49ers will not hesitate to capitalize. Dallas has to avoid those situations at all costs. The good news is they may have hit the quota for blue sweatpants and stocking cap unsportsmanlike conduct penalties for the season, so we can probably rule those out moving forward. item.description: Gasperini puts Balde talks with Barcelona on hold Roma has other priorities and is not making any moves for Alejandro Balde, at least for now. With January fast approaching, Tony D’Amico is working to identify reinforcements to make available to Gasperini. item.title: ‘Put on the coach’s shirt’ – When Pat Riley attacked David Stern’s $25,000 fine over Magic Johnson
item.description: Photo by Focus on Sport/Getty Images NBA legend Pat Riley once dropped a vicious take on a $25,000 fine by then-commissioner David Stern. Today, Pat Riley is known as the Godfather of the NBA and continues to be a crucial decision-maker for the Miami Heat. While Riley also played in the NBA, he climbed the ladder of success during his tenure as the head coach of the Los Angeles Lakers during the ‘Showtime era.’ A key reason behind Riley’s success was his outspoken nature, which he flaunted when the Lakers were handed a $25,000 fine for resting star guard Magic Johnson. (Original Caption) Boston: Los Angeles Lakers coach Pat Riley raises his fist as the Lakers take the lead and go on to win game 4 in the final seconds to defeat Boston, 107-106. Lakers now lead series, 3-1. Pat Riley called out David Stern’s $25,000 fine in 1989 The story dates back to the 1989 regular season, when the Lakers had already clinched the No. 1 seed in the Western Conference. To ensure that the Lakers stars stayed fresh for the postseason after an injury-ridden season, Riley rested Johnson, James Worthy, and Mychal Thompson for the final regular-season game. However, this didn’t sit well with then-NBA commissioner David Stern, who slapped the Lakers with a $25,000 fine. Despite that, Riley didn’t back down and instead went off at Stern. “I have an obligation to our management. I decide who the h___ I want to play. If [the league] is going to start getting in the way of who I want to play and when I want to play them, maybe they ought to come out here and put on the coach’s shirt themselves,” Riley said, per Deseret News . He added, “I’m sort of beside myself on this. Obviously, a new rule has been made, a new precedent set. I didn’t do it out of disregard for the league. I did it for the well-being of our players. “They do it [rest starters in meaningless games] in other sports.” Late LA Lakers owner Dr. Jerry Buss did apologize for how his team treated the final game of the season as Portland Trail Blazers fans were left fuming. After all, the fans paid a lot of money to attend the game, only to find that the big stars were rested by Riley. The Lakers icon did end up apologizing as well, but he maintained his stance that the game was insignificant for the team in the grand scheme of things. item.title: Jon Jones cheers as Ciryl Gane takes out hater Josh Hokit at UFC 334
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - MARCH 03: (L-R) Opponents Jon Jones and Ciryl Gane of France face off during the UFC 285 ceremonial weigh-in at MGM Grand Garden Arena on March 03, 2023 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Jon Jones may train under the same coaches as Josh Hokit, but he is not a fan of the heavyweight contender. Hokit dropped a close decision to current heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane at UFC 334 on Saturday night, pushing a wild pace on “Bon Gamin” but fading through the fourth and fifth rounds en route to a 48-47 unanimous decision defeat. Pretty much everyone who watched the fight walked away impressed with Hokit’s performance (watch the highlights here) … but not Jones. “Same coaches, different results,” Jones said, referencing his win over Gane from 2023. “Put your hand down [Hokit]. Good job Frenchman!” Jon "Bones" Jones congratulates Cyril Gane's win over Josh Hokit #ufc334 pic.twitter.com/nyt7EXY6SY — Mosheki Daniel (@MoshekiD) November 15, 2026 Despite both being trained by Greg Jackson and Mike Winkeljohn, there’s growing animosity between Jones and Hokit. Hokit was one of the louder voices bashing Jones after his protege Gable Steveson got knocked out in September. “It’s the craziest coincidence,” Jones wrote on X (formerly Twitter). “Almost every single fighter that talks crap about me ends up losing the next fight. I swear it’s been that way for years. Weird.” Jones’ two-minute clowning of Gane has certainly aged well now that the French fighter has claimed the undisputed heavyweight title, defeating Alex Pereira and Josh Hokit.
